title: Closing the Digital Divide for SGUnited: Learnings from COVID-19
what_it_is: Closing the Digital Divide for SGUnited: Learnings from COVID-19

sections.label: Household computer and Internet access
sections.summary: 81% of resident households have a personal computer and 87% have Internet access, with 45% of 1- and 2-room HDB households having Internet access.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Only 81% of resident households have a personal computer, and only 87% have Internet access.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Only 45% of households residing in 1- and 2-room HDB flats have Internet access.

sections.label: MOE loaned devices
sections.summary: MOE has loaned out an estimated 20,000 devices, including laptops and tablets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MOE has loaned out an estimated 20,000 devices, including laptops and tablets.

sections.label: NEU PC Plus Scheme
sections.summary: The Government introduced the NEU PC Plus Scheme in 2006, offering students and PWDs from low-income households a new personal computer with three years of free internet connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government intervened by introducing the NEU PC Plus Scheme in 2006, offering students and PWDs from low-income households a new personal computer bundled with three years of free internet connectivity.

sections.label: Secondary 1 students devices timeline
sections.summary: The Minister for Education said that by 2024 every Secondary 1 student will have a tablet, laptop, or chromebook, and the Deputy Prime Minister shared this timeline will be accelerated earlier.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Minister for Education has said that, by 2024, every Secondary 1 student will have a tablet, a laptop, or a chromebook, which the Deputy Prime Minister just shared that this timeline will be accelerated earlier.

sections.label: Digital Readiness Blueprint commitment
sections.summary: MCI committed in its Digital Readiness Blueprint that all Singaporeans will be digitally ready, no matter their income or current IT abilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MCI has boldly committed in its Digital Readiness Blueprint that all Singaporeans will be digitally ready, no matter their income or current IT abilities.

sections.label: Digital Empowerment Voucher scheme proposal
sections.summary: The passage asks whether a Digital Empowerment Voucher scheme combining aspects of the Public Transport Voucher and Innovation & Capability Voucher schemes can reduce time and resources to deliver digital devices to families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To reduce the time and resources required to deliver digital devices to families, can we have a Digital Empowerment Voucher (DEV) scheme that combines aspects of the existing Public Transport Voucher and Innovation & Capability Voucher schemes?

sections.label: Universal Internet access as utility
sections.summary: The Framework states universal Internet access should be provided as a public utility, especially for low-income households.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Within this Framework, universal Internet access should be provided as a public utility especially for low-income households.

sections.label: Gathering digital divide statistics
sections.summary: Meaningful statistics across more diverse groups should be gathered regularly, citing the UK Office for National Statistics' digital divide studies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Meaningful statistics and metrics across more diversed groups should be gathered regularly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the UK, for example, the Office for the National Statistics studies the digital divide across locations, gender, age, income, disability, ethnic groups and language, education and other social and economic determinants of digital inequality.

sections.label: Including vulnerable groups in digital policy
sections.summary: The speaker urges Government to include vulnerable groups' views in digital policy and proposes a Citizen's Workgroup.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I therefore want to conclude by imploring the Government to ensure that every digital policy design intentionally includes the views and experiences from our vulnerable groups, these digital outcasts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I propose that a Citizen's Workgroup be established comprising citizens and community groups to complement the Digital Readiness Workgroup made up of leaders in public, people and private sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Like the MOH's commitment that "no Singaporean will be denied appropriate care because of an inability to pay", the Digital Readiness Blueprint takes the position that "no Singaporean will be denied adequate digital access because of an inability to pay, or use".

sections.label: Digital access as public utility
sections.summary: A commentary proposes a paradigm shift to regard digital access as a public utility, like electricity and water.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In my commentary published in ChannelNewsAsia today, co-authored with Assoc Prof Irene Ng from the National University of Singapore, we propose a significant paradigm shift – to regard digital access as a public utility, just as we do electricity and water.

sections.label: Extending free home wi-fi
sections.summary: With the Nationwide Broadband Network in place, extending free home wi-fi requires coordination with telcos outfitting homes with modems and routers.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With our Nationwide Broadband Network successfully in place, extending free home wi-fi to residential areas will not involve more than a concerted coordination with telcos outfitting every home with modems and wireless routers.

sections.label: Universal provision of computing devices
sections.summary: Universal provision of computing devices assumes need with less concern over deservingness, allowing automatic allocation like Baby Bonus, WIS and Silver Support.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Universal provision of computing devices assumes need with less concern over deservingness.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thus, greater universalism could materialise in the form of automatic allocation, as is the case now with Baby Bonus, Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) and Silver Support.

sections.label: Universal digital access as utility
sections.summary: It states that making universal digital access an affordable public utility is the best way to ensure everyone gets on the social mobility escalator.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun
sentences.text: The best way to ensure that everyone gets on the social mobility escalator is to make universal digital access an affordable public utility.

sections.label: Household computer ownership survey
sections.summary: IMDA's 2019 Annual Infocomm Usage Survey found 89% of all households and 98% of households with school-going children own computers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: IMDA's Annual Infocomm Usage Survey in 2019 found that 89% of all households own computers; and among households with school-going children, 98% own computers.

sections.label: Singapore broadband subscription rates
sections.summary: It states Singapore's 3G and 4G mobile broadband subscription rate is 100% of the mobile market and total broadband is 807 per 1,000 population.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Our 3G and 4G mobile broadband subscription rate stands at 100% of the total mobile market, compared with an international average of 75%; and our total broadband which is fixed and mobile subscribers, stand at 807 per 1,000 of population, compared to an international average of 369 per 1,000.

sections.label: NEU PC Plus programme help
sections.summary: Since 2006, IMDA's NEU PC Plus programme has helped over 46,000 low-income households with school-going children or persons with disabilities obtain computers and broadband access.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: For example, since 2006, IMDA's NEU PC Plus programme, which Members have all referred to, has helped over 46,000 low-income households, with school-going children or persons with disabilities, for them to obtain computers and broadband access.

sections.label: MOE devices for home-based learning
sections.summary: During Home-based Learning, MOE loaned out more than 20,000 computing devices and 1,600 Internet-enabling devices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: During the period of Home-based Learning (HBL), for example, Members have already heard how MOE loaned out more than 20,000 computing devices and 1,600 Internet-enabling devices.

sections.label: Adapted NEU PC Plus programme
sections.summary: IMDA adapted the NEU PC Plus programme so families with three or more school-going children could apply for a second subsidised PC, with over 3,000 computers given out.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In terms of the NEU PC Plus programme, for example, what IMDA did was then to adapt the programme so that families with three or more school-going children could apply for a second subsidised PC and more than 3,000 computers were given out in this period despite the supply chain restrictions that we had to deal with.

sections.label: Digital inclusion efforts and partnerships
sections.summary: The passage states efforts with seniors, hawkers and low-income households aim for universality in digital inclusion, with community and corporate partners, so every Singaporean is digitally ready.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: As Ms Ong noted, the group Engineering Good has been collecting and refurbishing 1,800 old laptops for those who cannot afford one of their own and I also know that they have been working with partners like Progress NEST and A Good Space, whom Ms Ong is associated with and I think we will continue to encourage such collaborations amongst the community organisations and between the public and private sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I want to conclude by highlighting again, as Deputy Prime Minister has highlighted, we want to build on these momentum, including the various initiatives for seniors, to reach out to all segments.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, the efforts with seniors, the efforts with hawkers, the efforts with low-income households, they are all a measure of our aspiration to ensure universality in the approach we take towards digital inclusion.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But, it is a challenging task as I am sure Members like Prof Lim who has been involved in some of these community efforts know, as you go further down, it becomes harder and harder to implement.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We welcome this and we will do our utmost to ensure that every Singaporean is digitally ready and we will work with community and corporate partners and canvas widely for ideas as has been suggested by both Members.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Our ultimate goal is to ensure that every Singaporean regardless of age income or background is well prepared to lead a fulfilling life in our shared digital future.
